name: Basilica of St. John, Des Moines
history: The parish's first Mass was on Christmas Day 1905. A basement church was finished in 1913 and used until the upper church was completed. The present church, by Maginnis & Walsh of Boston, was dedicated on 4 December 1927. It became a basilica in 1989.
arch: Romanesque Revival in Indiana limestone. The architects had suggested brick to save money, but the pastor, Father McNamara, insisted on limestone and raised the funds. The design draws on St. Paul Outside the Walls in Rome.
features: The baldachin and high altar by Maginnis & Walsh were added in 1929.
Conrad Pickel Studio designed the 10 nave windows and 36 clerestory windows, installed from 1947 to 1953.

look.d: An Italian-style bell tower stands beside the church.
The design looks to the Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls in Rome.

fun: The same Boston architects designed the National Shrine in Washington, D.C.
journal: A pastor who wouldn't settle for brick. Limestone it was.

quiz.q: Why is it limestone, not brick?
a: The pastor insisted and raised the money

quiz.q: Where was the first Mass of the parish held?
